{"full_contract_with_original_span_markers":"<SPAN 0>NON-COMPETITION AND NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT</SPAN 0>
<SPAN 1>This NON-COMPETITION AND NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT dated this 6th day of August, 2003 (this "AGREEMENT"), is made and entered into by and between HARRISON S. TRASK ("PRINCIPAL"), PHOENIX FOOTWEAR GROUP, INC., a Delaware corporation ("PHOENIX FOOTWEAR"), and its wholly-owned subsidiary PFG ACQUISITION, INC., a Montana corporation ("PFG ACQUISITION").</SPAN 1>
<SPAN 2>A. Phoenix Footwear, PFG Acquisition and H.S. Trask & Co., a Montana corporation ("COMPANY"), have entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger, dated June 16, 2003 (the "MERGER AGREEMENT"), pursuant to which Company shall merge with and into Acquisition Sub and the separate corporate existence of Company shall cease.</SPAN 2>
<SPAN 3>B. Principal is employed as President and Chief Executive Officer of Company and serves as a director of the Company.</SPAN 3>
<SPAN 4>C. It is mutually agreed between Principal, Company and PFG Acquisition that Principal shall resign his employment as President and Chief Executive Officer of Company and as a director, said resignation to take effect as of the date that the Merger between Company and PFG Acquisition becomes effective (the "MERGER EFFECTIVE DATE").</SPAN 4>
<SPAN 5>D. It is also mutually agreed between Principal, Company and PFG Acquisition that Principal shall be employed as an employee of the surviving corporation to the Merger ("SURVIVING CORPORATION") from the Merger Effective Date to December 31, 2003 and thereafter as a consultant until December 31, </SPAN 5><SPAN 6>2005. Principal and Surviving Corporation have accordingly entered into an Employment and Consulting Agreement dated August 6, 2003 (the "EMPLOYMENT AND CONSULTING AGREEMENT").</SPAN 6>
<SPAN 7>E. Principal owns approximately 38% of the outstanding voting securities of the Company, and will receive considerable financial benefit when the Merger becomes effective.</SPAN 7>
<SPAN 8>F. The Merger Agreement requires that Principal, Phoenix Footwear and PFG Acquisition enter into this Agreement.</SPAN 8>
<SPAN 9>NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the foregoing, and of the respective representations, warranties, covenants and agreements contained herein, the parties agree as follows (unless otherwise defined herein, capitalized terms used herein shall have the meanings given such terms in the Merger Agreement):</SPAN 9>
<SPAN 10>1. EFFECTIVE DATE. </SPAN 10><SPAN 11>This Agreement shall take effect on the Merger Effective Date.</SPAN 11>
<SPAN 12>2. NON-COMPETITION. </SPAN 12><SPAN 13>In order to induce Phoenix Footwear and PFG Acquisition to enter into the Merger Agreement and to pay the valuable consideration required thereunder, to create a valuable independent asset of PFG Acquisition, to preserve and protect the goodwill thereof, and to enhance the going concern value and earnings of PFG Acquisition in future years, Principal undertakes and agrees as follows:</SPAN 13>
<SPAN 14>(a) Commencing on the effective date hereof and continuing thereafter until December 31, 2005 (the "RESTRICTION PERIOD"), Principal shall not, within the United States (the "TERRITORY"), create, seek or accept employment or compensation of any kind or character from any enterprise, or person associated with any enterprise that is engaged or planning to engage, directly or indirectly, in the manufacture, sale, marketing, promotion or sale of products in the brown shoe market segment of the men's footwear business (a "COMPETING ENTERPRISE"); provided, however, that Principal may accept employment as a salesman or as a sales representative with any such Competing Enterprise without violating the foregoing.</SPAN 14>
<SPAN 15>(b) During the Term, neither Principal nor any entity in which Principal may be interested (as a principal, owner, partner, joint venturer, trustee, director, officer, shareholder, option holder, security holder, lender, creditor, guarantor, advisor, member or in any other capacity other than solely as a salesman or as a sales representative) shall, within the Territory, engage, directly or indirectly, in any activity that, directly or indirectly, manufactures, markets, promotes or engages in the sale of products in the brown shoe market segment of the men's footwear business; provided, however, that the foregoing shall not be deemed to prevent Principal from investing in securities if </SPAN 15><SPAN 16>(i) such class of securities in which the investment so made is listed on a national securities exchange or is issued by a company registered under Section 12(g) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, so long as such investment holdings do not, in the aggregate, constitute more than five percent (5%) of the voting power of the entity issuing such securities; and </SPAN 16><SPAN 17>(ii) any other securities so long as such investment holdings do not constitute more than two percent (2%) of the voting power of the entity issuing such securities.</SPAN 17>
<SPAN 18>(c) During the Term, without the Company's written consent, Principal shall not, either in his individual capacity or as an agent for another: </SPAN 18><SPAN 19>(i) hire or offer to hire any of Company's, Phoenix Footwear's or PFG Acquisition's officers, employees, or agents; </SPAN 19><SPAN 20>(ii) entice away or in any other manner persuade or attempt to persuade any of Company's, Phoenix Footwear's or PFG Acquisition's officers, employees, or agents to discontinue their relationship with Company, Phoenix Footwear or PFG Acquisition; </SPAN 20><SPAN 21>(iii) contract, solicit, divert, or attempt to divert from Phoenix Footwear or PFG Acquisition any business whatsoever by influencing or attempting to influence any customer of Company, Phoenix Footwear or PFG Acquisition with whom Company, Phoenix Footwear or PFG Acquisition has engaged in sales discussions prior to the termination of this Agreement; or </SPAN 21><SPAN 22>(iv) contract, solicit, divert, or attempt to divert from Company, Phoenix Footwear or PFG Acquisition any supplier or vendor.</SPAN 22>
<SPAN 23>(d) The covenants set forth in this Section 2 shall be construed as a series of separate covenants covering their subject matter in each of the separate states within the Territory and, except for geographic coverage, each such separate covenant shall be deemed identical in terms to the covenant set forth above in this Section 2. </SPAN 23><SPAN 24>To the extent that any such covenant shall be judicially unenforceable in any one or more of such states, such covenant shall not be affected with respect to each of the other states in the Territory. </SPAN 24><SPAN 25>Each covenant with respect to each such state in the Territory shall be construed as severable and independent.</SPAN 25>
<SPAN 26>(e) Phoenix Footwear, PGG </SPAN 26><SPAN 27>Acquisition and Principal acknowledge and recognize that these covenants not to compete are integral to the Merger Agreement, that without the protection of such covenants, Phoenix Footwear and PFG Acquisition would not have entered into the Merger Agreement, that the consideration paid by Phoenix Footwear and PFG Acquisition under the Merger Agreement bears no relationship to the damages Phoenix Footwear and PFG Acquisition may suffer in the event of any breach of the covenants, and that such covenants contain reasonable limitations as to time, geographical area and scope of activity to be restrained necessary to protect Phoenix Footwear's and PFG Acquisition's business interests. </SPAN 27><SPAN 28>If this Section 2 shall for any reason be held excessively broad as to time, duration, geographical scope, activity or subject, it shall be enforceable to the extent compatible with then-applicable laws.</SPAN 28>
<SPAN 29>3. CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION.</SPAN 29>
<SPAN 30>(a) The parties acknowledge and agree that:</SPAN 30>
<SPAN 31>(i) The Company assets being merged into PFG Acquisition pursuant to the Merger Agreement include confidential and proprietary information of Company and, in the course of his employment for PFT Acquisition, Principal may develop and obtain access to confidential and proprietary information of Phoenix Footwear and PFG Acquisition (collectively, the "CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION"), which Confidential Information shall include, without limitation, all of the following materials and information of Company, Phoenix Footwear or PFG Acquisition (whether or not reduced to writing and whether or not patentable or protected by copyright): trade secrets, product specifications, proprietary software systems, sources of data, databases, know-how, formulae, inventions and ideas, designs, sketches, photographs, graphs, drawings, samples, selling and pricing information, procedures, research methodologies, customer lists, business and marketing plans, current and anticipated customer requirements, market studies, supplier lists, operational methods, product development plans and personnel plans. </SPAN 31><SPAN 32>The parties hereto agree that the failure of any Confidential Information to be marked or otherwise labeled as confidential or proprietary information shall not affect its status as Confidential Information.</SPAN 32>
<SPAN 33>(ii) The Confidential Information is confidential and proprietary, and the development and protection of the Confidential Information represents a substantial investment having a great economic and commercial value to Phoenix Footwear and PFG Acquisition.</SPAN 33>
<SPAN 34>(iii) Phoenix Footwear and PFG Acquisition would be irreparably damaged if any of the Confidential Information was disclosed to, or used or exploited on behalf of, any person other than Phoenix Footwear or PFG Acquisition.</SPAN 34>
<SPAN 35>(b) Principal covenants and agrees that he shall not, at any time, during the Restrictions Period, directly or indirectly, use, exploit, or disclose to any person or entity, without the prior written consent of Phoenix Footwear or PFG Acquisition, any Confidential Information, except as expressly authorized by Phoenix Footwear or PFG Acquisition during the performance of Principal's duties for and with PFG Acquisition.</SPAN 35>
<SPAN 36>(c) Notwithstanding the foregoing, Principal may use, exploit, or disclose Confidential Information, but only to the extent that such Confidential Information </SPAN 36><SPAN 37>(i) is or becomes publicly known through no wrongful act of Principal; or </SPAN 37><SPAN 38>(ii) is disclosed pursuant to the requirement of a governmental agency or a court of law or otherwise required by operation of law, provided that Principal gives PFG Acquisition and Phoenix Footwear prompt written notice of such requirement prior to disclosure.</SPAN 38>
<SPAN 39>4. REASONABLENESS OF RESTRICTIONS. </SPAN 39><SPAN 40>PRINCIPAL HAS CAREFULLY READ AND CONSIDERED THE PROVISIONS OF SECTIONS 2 AND 3 HEREOF AND, HAVING DONE SO, HEREBY AGREES THAT THE RESTRICTIONS SET FORTH IN SUCH SECTIONS ARE FAIR AND REASONABLE AND ARE REASONABLY REQUIRED FOR THE PROTECTION OF THE INTERESTS OF PHOENIX FOOTWEAR AND PFG Acquisition.</SPAN 40>
<SPAN 41>5. INJUNCTIVE RELIEF.</SPAN 41>
<SPAN 42>(a) Principal acknowledges and agrees that Phoenix Footwear and PFG Acquisition will suffer irreparable harm in the event that Principal breaches any of its obligations under this Agreement, and that monetary damages shall be inadequate to compensate Phoenix Footwear and PFG Acquisition for any such breach. </SPAN 42><SPAN 43>Principal agrees that in the event of any breach or threatened breach by Principal of the provisions of this Agreement, Phoenix Footwear and PFG Acquisition, or either of them, shall be entitled to a temporary restraining order, preliminary injunction, and permanent injunction in order to prevent or restrain any such breach or threatened breach by Principal, or by any or all of Principal's agents, representatives or other persons directly or indirectly acting for, on behalf of, or with Principal.</SPAN 43>
<SPAN 44>(b) Notwithstanding the provisions set forth in Section 5(a) above, or any other provision contained in this Agreement, the parties hereby agree that no remedy conferred by any of the specific provisions of this Agreement, including without limitation, this Section 5, is intended to be exclusive of any other remedy, and each and every remedy shall be cumulative and shall be in addition to every other remedy given hereunder or now or hereafter existing at law or in equity or by statute or otherwise.</SPAN 44>
<SPAN 45>6. MISCELLANEOUS.</SPAN 45>
<SPAN 46>(a) Notices. </SPAN 46><SPAN 47>All notices required or permitted to be given under this Agreement shall be given by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the parties at the following addresses or such other addresses as any party may designate in writing to the other parties:</SPAN 47>
<SPAN 48>If to Phoenix Footwear or PFG Acquisition:</SPAN 48>
<SPAN 49>5759 Fleet Street, Suite 220</SPAN 49>
<SPAN 50>Carlsbad, California 92008</SPAN 50>
<SPAN 51>Attention: President and Chief Executive Officer</SPAN 51>
<SPAN 52>with a copy (which shall not constitute notice) to:</SPAN 52>
<SPAN 53>Gordon E. Forth, Esq.</SPAN 53>
<SPAN 54>Woods Oviatt Gilman LLP</SPAN 54>
<SPAN 55>700 Crossroads Building</SPAN 55>
<SPAN 56>2 State Street</SPAN 56>
<SPAN 57>Rochester, New York 14614</SPAN 57>
<SPAN 58>If to Principal:</SPAN 58>
<SPAN 59>101 Sourdough Ridge Road</SPAN 59>
<SPAN 60>Bozeman, Montana 59715</SPAN 60>
<SPAN 61>(b) Governing Law. </SPAN 61><SPAN 62>This Agreement shall be deemed to made in and in all respects shall be interpreted, construed, and governed by and in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware without regard to the conflicts of law principles thereof.</SPAN 62>
<SPAN 63>(c) Amendments. </SPAN 63><SPAN 64>This Agreement may be amended, supplemented, or modified only in writing, duly executed by all of the parties hereto.</SPAN 64>
<SPAN 65>(d) Non-waiver. </SPAN 65><SPAN 66>A delay or failure by any party to exercise a right under this Agreement, or a partial or single exercise of that right shall not constitute a waiver of that or any other right.</SPAN 66>
<SPAN 67>(e) Counterparts. </SPAN 67><SPAN 68>This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts, each such counterpart being deemed to be an original instrument, and all such counterparts shall together constitute the same agreement.</SPAN 68>
<SPAN 69>(f) Entire Agreement. </SPAN 69><SPAN 70>This Agreement, together with the Employment and Consulting Agreement, constitutes the entire agreement, and supersedes all other prior agreements, understandings, representations, and warranties both written and oral, among the parties, with respect to the subject matter hereof. </SPAN 70><SPAN 71>Each party to this Agreement acknowledges</SPAN 71>
<SPAN 72>that no representations, inducements, promises or agreements, orally or otherwise, have been made by any party or anyone acting on behalf of any party which are not embodied herein.</SPAN 72>
<SPAN 73>(g) Severability. </SPAN 73><SPAN 74>The provisions of this Agreement shall be deemed severable and the invalidity or unenforceability of any provision shall not affect the validity or enforceability of the other provisions hereof. </SPAN 74><SPAN 75>If any provision of this Agreement, or the application thereof to any person or any circumstance, is invalid or unenforceable, </SPAN 75><SPAN 76>(i) a suitable and equitable provision shall be substituted therefor in order to carry out, so far as may be valid and enforceable, the intent and purpose of such invalid or unenforceable provision; and </SPAN 76><SPAN 77>(ii) the remainder of this Agreement and the application of such provision to other persons or circumstances shall not be affected by such invalidity or unenforceability, nor shall such invalidity or unenforceability affect the validity or enforceability of such provision, or the application thereof, in any other jurisdiction.</SPAN 77>
<SPAN 78>(h) Binding Effect. </SPAN 78><SPAN 79>Principal may not assign any of his rights or delegate any of his duties or obligations under this Agreement. </SPAN 79><SPAN 80>The rights and obligations of Acquisition Sub and Company under this Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of their respective successors and assigns.</SPAN 80>
<SPAN 81>IN WITNESS WHEREOF, this Agreement has been duly executed and delivered by each of the parties hereto as of the date first written above.</SPAN 81>
<SPAN 82>PHOENIX FOOTWEAR GROUP, INC.</SPAN 82>
<SPAN 83>By: /s/ James Riedman</SPAN 83>

guidance.when: Assessing whether return or destruction is required when the agreement or protected evaluation ends.
guidance.inspection: Identify both the required act and its trigger. Termination, expiration, conclusion of an evaluation, a determination that development cannot proceed, or cessation of interest qualifies when that event itself activates the duty. A request-only duty does not qualify. Nor does a party's unilateral decision not to proceed unless the clause treats that decision as the operative conclusion of the protected process.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the complete return-or-destruction duty together with its end-event trigger. Do not omit a governing introduction, and do not substitute a request trigger or a retention clause for the required end-event link.

guidance.when: The agreement contains an exception to a return or destruction obligation.
guidance.inspection: Check whether the exception expressly permits continued possession of backups, archival material, a legal copy, or another defined subset after the return/destruction event. Conditions on access, purpose, or continuing confidentiality do not negate the permission.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the retention exception and, when separated, the governing return/destruction clause showing the temporal context.

guidance.when: The agreement requires return or destruction of confidential information and copies without stating a retention exception.
guidance.inspection: Determine whether the duty is exhaustive as to the covered material and copies. A complete return/destruction command that leaves no authorized retained subset negates permission to possess some material afterward.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the exhaustive operative duty and verify across the complete agreement that no backup, archival, legal-copy, or other retention exception qualifies it.

guidance.when: The agreement addresses ownership, licenses, or rights in confidential information or associated intellectual property.
guidance.inspection: Look for language that no license or right is granted, conveyed, conferred, or implied. A limited authorization to review or use information for the stated transaction does not by itself contradict the broader no-grant proposition.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the express no-grant clause; include an ownership clause only when it helps establish the object of the denied rights.

guidance.when: The agreement restricts disclosure of negotiations, discussions, a contemplated transaction, the agreement itself, or the existence of dealings.
guidance.inspection: A prohibition on revealing that negotiations or discussions exist establishes the hypothesis. A prohibition on public announcements concerning the agreement or transaction also qualifies; definition text alone must be paired with an operative nondisclosure duty.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative prohibition and the protected fact, retaining any governing introduction needed to connect a listed fact to the prohibition.

guidance.when: Confidential-information coverage is conditioned on marking, designation, or identification by the disclosing party.
guidance.inspection: Confirm that the identification condition grammatically governs every covered disclosure mode. A single terminal condition may govern an enumeration of oral, written, and electronic modes; different procedures may also govern different modes. Do not treat nature- or circumstances-based coverage as identification.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the complete definition or all clauses needed to show that every disclosure mode is subject to identification by the disclosing party.

guidance.when: The definition covers information either expressly designated confidential or reasonably understood to be confidential from its nature or disclosure circumstances.
guidance.inspection: The contextual alternative independently covers undesignated information, so express identification by the disclosing party is not required for all confidential information.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the complete alternative definition showing both designation and circumstance- or nature-based coverage.

guidance.when: Assessing whether the receiving party may make a copy in some circumstance.
guidance.inspection: Require an affirmative operational route for making copies, such as copies necessary for an authorized purpose or acknowledged backup creation. Prepared analyses or compilations do not by themselves authorize copying. A ban qualified by prior consent, and a remedy for unauthorized copying, are not affirmative permissions.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the language that affirmatively authorizes, requires, or acknowledges copy creation and its condition; access, disclosure, derivative-document coverage, consent qualifiers, and breach-remedy clauses are insufficient.

guidance.when: The agreement prohibits copying confidential information and contains no affirmative operational copying route.
guidance.inspection: A direct copy ban, including a ban stated as applying without prior consent or approval, negates the benchmark permission hypothesis when the complete agreement does not otherwise authorize necessary copies, backups, or another copying circumstance. Do not convert the consent qualifier itself into affirmative permission.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the copy prohibition and verify across the agreement that no affirmative operational-copy or backup route qualifies it.

guidance.when: The agreement permits disclosure to representatives or other persons.
guidance.inspection: Resolve who falls within the permitted class. Consultants, agents, counsel, accountants, professional advisers, affiliates, and similar non-employees establish sharing with some third parties; an employee-only exception does not.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite both the permission and the definition or enumeration proving that at least one permitted recipient is a third party, plus any need-to-know or confidentiality condition governing the permission.

guidance.when: The agreement states an authorized transaction, project, evaluation, business relationship, or other defined purpose for confidential information.
guidance.inspection: A command to use confidential information only for that purpose, or not for any other purpose, directly imposes the limited-use obligation. The existence of the authorized purpose is not a contradiction.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative use restriction and enough purpose language to identify the authorized scope.

guidance.when: Relevant candidate text is a numbered item, exception, continuation, anaphoric clause, or otherwise incomplete fragment.
guidance.inspection: Read the governing introduction and adjacent items to determine the item's legal function, trigger, subject, and exceptions. Keep independent operative clauses separately; do not treat a neighboring item as evidence merely because it shares the list.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include every span necessary to make the relied-on proposition complete, while excluding sibling items that do not establish that proposition.

guidance.when: The confidential-information definition enumerates subject matter or data categories.
guidance.inspection: Find an expressly covered non-technical category, such as business, financial, marketing, personnel, customer, contact, or transaction information. Generic references to all information, documents, analyses, form, or derivatives do not alone prove non-technical coverage.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the definition and at least one explicit non-technical category; include continuation text when the category list crosses fragments.

guidance.when: The agreement contains an exclusion, reservation, or acknowledgment concerning independent development.
guidance.inspection: Confirm that the receiving party may develop information independently without using or accessing the protected information. Prior approval to disclose, lawful receipt, or another unrelated exception does not establish independent development.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the independent-development clause with its governing exclusion or reservation language when needed to make its legal function complete.

guidance.when: The agreement addresses information obtained from an external source or later made available non-confidentially.
guidance.inspection: Require lawful receipt from a source other than the disclosing party or its representatives, with the source free of confidentiality restrictions, or a later non-confidential release that makes the information externally available. Independent development is different. Information supplied by a third-party vendor through the disclosing party is still disclosed through the protected channel and is not an acquisition permission.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the external-source or non-confidential-release item and its governing exclusion introduction, including the condition on the source's authority or confidentiality duty.

guidance.when: The definition or coverage clause addresses communication form.
guidance.inspection: Determine whether oral or verbal communication is expressly within confidential information, including language covering information irrespective of communication form or information disclosed in writing and also orally. Do not infer oral coverage merely from derivative notes or documents.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the language linking oral, verbal, or form-independent communication to confidential-information coverage, with any necessary definition continuation.

guidance.when: The agreement restricts recruiting, hiring, employment contact, or solicitation involving personnel of the disclosing party.
guidance.inspection: Find a prohibition on soliciting, employing, hiring, or initiating employment contact with officers, employees, or other personnel. Proxy solicitation, transaction standstill language, and general contact restrictions are not personnel nonsolicitation unless tied to employment or hiring.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative employment-related prohibition and the covered personnel class; include duration, targeting limits, or recruiting exceptions when they qualify the prohibition.

guidance.when: The agreement states that duties continue beyond an end event or remain effective for a post-event period.
guidance.inspection: Verify that confidentiality, non-use, or another agreement obligation continues after termination, expiration, completion, abandonment, or an equivalent end of the protected relationship. Continuation merely after return or destruction does not establish survival of agreement termination.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite both the continuing obligation and the termination, expiration, completion, abandonment, or equivalent end event to which continuation is linked.

guidance.when: The agreement permits disclosure or access to employees, internal staff, or a defined representative class.
guidance.inspection: Confirm an operative permission and that employees or internal staff belong to the permitted class. A definition naming employees is insufficient without a disclosure route; a permission to consultants, agents, or affiliates alone does not establish employee sharing.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the disclosure or access permission and, if the permission uses a defined class, the definition proving employees are included, plus material need-to-know or confidentiality conditions.

guidance.when: A clause permits or addresses disclosure compelled by law, regulation, court order, governmental demand, or legal process.
guidance.inspection: Determine whether that compelled-disclosure event requires notice, consultation, or equivalent advance communication to the disclosing party, subject to any legal-permission qualifier. A compelled-disclosure exception without a communication duty is insufficient, as is notice of an unauthorized disclosure after it occurs.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite both the compelled-disclosure trigger and the notice or consultation duty, including cross-referenced or list-introduction text needed to connect them.

guidance.when: The agreement affirmatively permits use of confidential information or defined residual information beyond a transaction-specific or otherwise stated agreement purpose.
guidance.inspection: A permission to use protected information for any purpose, or for the recipient's general internal business purposes without tying use to the agreement's stated purpose, negates an exclusive-purpose restriction. Merely allowing copying, disclosure, or conduct of a proposed relationship does not establish this contradiction.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the affirmative broad-use permission and any definition needed to show that it applies to confidential information or information retained from it.

guidance.when: The agreement states who may receive confidential information and the exception is limited to employees.
guidance.inspection: If disclosure is prohibited to everyone except qualifying employees, and the complete agreement supplies no permission for consultants, agents, advisers, or other non-employees, the agreement negates permission to share with third parties. A consent-based possibility alone is not an existing sharing permission.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the employee-only exception and the governing prohibition, and verify that no independent non-employee disclosure route qualifies it.
